title: Residential and home care run by organizations the City pays
question: Do organizations paid by the City run licensed residential or home-care sites that are on probation, closed or seriously cited?
finding: The State files list 9 children's 24-hour residential licences, 73 adult residential and adult day-program, 74 elder-care and 57 home-care licences in San Francisco. 43 are held by an organization the City paid in fiscal 2025 or 2026. 2 San Francisco licences in these files are on probation, none held by a City payee. Unity Care Group (Unity Care Group, transitional housing placement program, licensed): 4 Type A citations and 9 upheld complaint allegations. San Francisco Boys And Girls/ Shelter (Catholic Charities, short term residential therapeutic program, licensed): 3 Type A citations and 5 upheld complaint allegations. Peter Claver Community (Catholic Charities, residential facility chronically ill, licensed): 4 Type A citations and 1 upheld complaint allegations.
how: Every San Francisco licence in the four State files was matched by licensee name to City-paid nonprofit profiles and, failing that, to a City payee with the same name (letters and digits only). City payments are fiscal 2025 plus 2026 by the year of the voucher number, all departments. Licences held by people in their own name are left out unless the name is a City-paid nonprofit.
limits: The City's payment may be for a different program than the licensed site. A name match is labelled as such. Probation and citations are the licensing office's findings, not court rulings. Many small adult homes are run by individuals and are not shown.
